change_log.Description: Register created for the AKOS catalogue. Seeded with the three tools published in this repository. This register is itself an instance of TSP.3.
TSP.4 Tool Installer registered. First entry with no skill - recorded to show the register handles tools whose value is not an agent interface.
TSP.5 registered. Generalised from a personal reference-material system and a per-project document control list that turned out to be one tool at two scopes.

td-author added as TSP.3's second skill. The catalogue published the TD template and the reasoning behind it, but nothing that operationalised either - the boundary between a TD and a SKILL.md, and where history goes inside a TD, were documented as method and enforced nowhere.
Registered as TSP.6. First tool published with no code and with shared material: its skills read contracts from _shared/, which install.py now copies beside the skill.
Registered as TSP.7. Second tool with no code. Ships an empty notebooks tree and a post template as assets/, so a fresh install builds what it needs on first use.
Registered as TSP.8. The first ceremony tool: two skills and a record script, using TSP.1-3 together. Ships register-only; TD.8 says where a tracker and a calendar plug in.
Registered as TSP.9. Second ceremony tool: two skills and a shared day record, no code. The evening runs TSP.8's status check each day.

TD.6 v2.0: content runs on the WBS. Plans name the goal they serve; a committed piece has a row in the WBS of that goal's owner and carries a dated status and a WBS Ref; start, publish and drop propose the matching WBS change. Stage, activation, commitment write-back, campaign scoring and sprints.md retired. New dependency on TSP.1.
TD.10 v1.0: published. Needs TSP.1 and TSP.8 (structured goals, TD.8 v1.2); reads TSP.2's Changes and Trend (TD.2 v1.5).

TD.1 v1.6: a Current Sprint board on the dashboard, lanes by the deliverable each card serves; a commitment means Not Started, and check warns on a committed row left in the backlog; add takes set's status stamps. sprint_populations() and sprint_board() are shared with reporting.
TD.2 v1.5: Change entries answered by Outcome, and the DRI's Trend on risks and issues; a Changes tab and a Trend column on the dashboard; migrate adds both to an older register.

TD.8 v1.2: sprint goals become data - ID, Done when, Bet, Carried from; committed items carry Area and Goal; the review answers each goal by ID; sprint_record.py goals reads them back. A commitment means Not Started.

TD.10 v1.1: the status report opens with the project's outcome and measures, read from its brief (templates/Project-Brief-template.md, new); On Outcome proposed and confirmed like the four, not counted in Overall.
TD.11 v1.0: the weekly review published as TSP.11, run on the day records, the sprint records and the registers alone.
TD.9 v1.2: the evening checks the weekly records (TSP.11) and says in one line when none is newer than seven days, silent until the first; A weekly review leaves Adapting it to your tools.
TSP.12 published: the action tracker, re-scoped for a team, with dated updates and the TBD checkpoint in the Due date cell from its dry run.
TD.11 v1.1: Waiting on someone also reads the action trackers (TSP.12): rows owed by others that are overdue, or TBD with no checkpoint or a passed one, three at most.
TSP.13 published: the stakeholder register, found by meta.kind under a root, the sprint calendar from the project's own conventions or WBS, contacts checked against git.

tools.Description: Work breakdown / backlog register per project: decomposition, effort, acceptance criteria, sprint allocation, with a generated dashboard.
tools.Name: WBS Register
tools.Notes: Ready to adopt. Template ships inside the skill folder.

tools.Description: Risks, Actions, Issues, Decisions and Ideas per project, with a probability x severity heat map and a generated dashboard.
tools.Name: RAID Register
tools.Notes: Ready to adopt. Register is built programmatically; no template file.

tools.Description: The inventory of tools, systems and procedures, plus the recurring controls that keep them alive. The spine of the method - this register is an instance of it. Automated by two skills: one owns the register row, the other owns the tool definition documents.
tools.Name: TSP Register
tools.Notes: Ready to adopt. Open item: Primary Area vocabulary resolved.

tools.Description: Vendors a tool from this catalogue into a project, records where the copy came from, and keeps it reconcilable with upstream: drift detection and three-way updates.
tools.Name: Tool Installer
tools.Notes: Ready to adopt. No skill by design - it runs at moments where a human decides.

tools.Description: Inventory of the artifacts belonging to a scope - documents, folders, tools and physical items - recording what each is, where it lives digitally and physically, what contains it, and which tool governs its contents. The register assigns an ID that is written onto the artifact itself, so its claims about the filesystem can be checked.
tools.Name: Artifact Register
tools.Notes: Ready to adopt. The only tool here that reconciles against reality rather than itself.

tools.Description: Turns thinking into finished, publish-ready pieces through interview rather than one-shot generation. Holds a position per scope, plans that name the goal they serve and hold a rate or an arc of pieces, an inbox for sparks, an interview-led writer, and a review that reports what was published against the rate and checks content against the WBS. Committed pieces run on the WBS Register (TSP.1). It is deliberately not a publisher: it stops at the finished piece and transmits to no platform.
tools.Name: Content System
tools.Notes: Implemented: used on real work, and improved as it is used. Runs on the WBS since v2.0 and needs wbs-manager installed beside it to commit pieces. Not everything is proven - its 27 quickstart scenarios predate the WBS design and have not been run, and no piece has yet gone through the full lifecycle; see TD.6, What is not proven.

tools.Description: Plain-Markdown notebooks the agent keeps: a diary, notebooks scoped to a project, an area of focus or an area of interest, and meeting notes, with an index per notebook. Raw entries worth more than a note can be crystallized into static HTML posts that link back to the entry they came from. No app, no search index, no database - files only.
tools.Name: Notebook Manager
tools.Notes: Usable: the diary and eDiary paths are used on real work, and a fresh install is tested. Meetings and scoped notebooks have never been exercised - see TD.7, Status. Personal by nature: install it in a personal workspace, or keep notebooks/ out of git.

tools.Description: The four sprint ceremonies - backlog grooming, the sprint close-out, the retrospective and sprint planning - run on the WBS, RAID and TSP registers alone, with one Markdown record per sprint written by sprint_record.py. Sprint state lives on WBS rows: staged by Horizon, committed by Sprint Planned, closed with a closure note. A task tracker and a calendar are described as adaptations, not configured.
tools.Name: Sprint Ceremonies
tools.Notes: Usable: the ceremonies run fortnightly on real work in their original setting. Register-only mode, as shipped, has been exercised on a scratch workspace but not yet on real work - see TD.8, Status. Needs wbs-manager; raid-manager and tsp-manager are optional.

tools.Description: The morning plan and the evening stand-up as one tool, sharing one Markdown record per day. The evening reviews the day from git, the WBS and the day's notes, raises a sprint ceremony that is due, chooses one to three frogs for tomorrow and closes the record; the morning confirms the frogs and opens the next. A calendar, a task tracker and inboxes are described as adaptations, not shipped.
tools.Name: Daily Loop
tools.Notes: Usable: the loop runs daily on real work in its original setting. Register-only mode, as shipped, has been exercised on a scratch workspace but not yet on real work - see TD.9, Status. No code; wbs-manager, sprint-facilitator and notebook-capture are each optional.

tools.Description: The project status report and the sprint update, each a JSON record and an HTML view generated from the WBS, RAID and the sprint records. The status report proposes the Essential 4 (On Time, On Scope, On Quality, Resources) with their evidence for the owner to confirm or override with a reason; the sprint update sets the last sprint's outcome beside the new sprint's commitments across projects, with the sprint's cards as a board on its own tab. Both open with an executive summary drafted in plain language and confirmed by the owner.
tools.Name: Reporting
tools.Notes: Usable: both reports run every sprint on real work in their original setting. As shipped here, exercised end to end on a scratch project built with AKOS's own tools, not yet on real work - see TD.10, Status. Needs wbs-manager and sprint-facilitator; raid-manager is optional.

tools.Description: The weekly level between the daily loop and the sprint, with its own Markdown record per review. It reads the week's day records, goes over the work beyond the sprint in the registers (rows falling due outside it, RAID entries past their review date), checks mid-sprint whether the sprint is on track and scans the open risks, places the week ahead, and routes what it finds rather than acting on it. A task tracker, a calendar, inboxes and a goal tracker are described as adaptations, not shipped.
tools.Name: Weekly Review
tools.Notes: Usable: the review runs weekly on real work in its original setting. Register-only mode, as shipped, has been walked through on a scratch workspace but not yet on real work - see TD.11, Status. No code; daily-loop-facilitator, sprint-facilitator, wbs-manager, raid-manager, reporting and notebook-capture are each optional.

tools.Description: A team's shared list of the small actions agreed in a piece of work's sessions, one Markdown file per piece of work, below the deliverables the WBS tracks and the governed items RAID holds. Every action whoever owes it, the owner named rather than assumed; filed in the support folder of the WBS row or RAID item it serves and indexed nowhere. No scripts. A personal task manager, a ticketing tool and meeting notes are described as adaptations, not shipped.
tools.Name: Action Tracker
tools.Notes: Not yet used on real work: walked through once on a scratch workspace, which added dated updates, the checkpoint in the Due date cell and a Status for closed actions - see TD.12, Status. No code; wbs-manager and raid-manager are optional, for the anchors and their folders.

tools.Description: For one project, who has a stake in it, where each stands and what flows to them: groups, stakeholders with power, interest and current against desired engagement, and a communications plan with each communication's audience, cadence, channel, share level and last sending. Resolves an audience to people and addresses at the moment of sending, says what is due or overdue, and generates a dashboard. Contacts per project in a CSV kept out of git, which the tool checks. Sends nothing.
tools.Name: Stakeholder Register
tools.Notes: Not yet used on real work: exercised by the smoke test on a scratch git project and by the made-up example register. The close-out's sending, the weekly review's check and the reporting tool's audiences are described but not yet run by those skills - see TD.13, Open items. Standard library; wbs-manager or an agile conventions file optional, for the sprint calendar.
